To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the morphologic and the dynamic characterization of histological verified breast lesions by gadoteric acid and by gadobutrol differ significantly.
the morphologic and kinetic characterization of histologically proven breast masses was different for gadoteric acid and for gadobutrot in an intraindividually performed breast MRI examination.
the 2 macrocyclical contrast media gadoteric acid and Gadobutol have similar diagnostic performance in terms of detection and morphologic and dynamic lesion characterization in breast MRI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comparison of 2 contrast agents, which are not yet approved for breast MRI in the United States.
the development of a computer-based system for the analysis and classification of breast MRI images.
the development of a new method for detecting breast cancer in the human breast.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gadoteric acid and Gadobutol have comparable performance for breast MRI.
the use of gadoteric acid or gadobutrol is not recommended as a single contrast agent for breast MRI.
the use of gadoteric acid for dynamic breast MRI is not recommended, whereas gadobenzoate (gadobutrol) is a good alternative to gadopentetate dimeglumine (gadoteric acid).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gadoteric acid and gado butrol are both reliable contrast media for breast DCE MRI.
gadoteric acid and the gadobutrol have different effects on dynamic enhancement and morphological characteristics of breast lesions.

both contrast agents are well suited for breast MRI, however with some differences in the dynamic and morphologic characteristics of breast lesions, and therefore the choice of contrast agent should be considered when planning a breast MRI examination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the standardization of MRI protocols is important for the interpretation of the results.
the choice of the contrast agent should be based on the individual patient and the indication.
gadoteric acid and gadoxetate disodium are not interchangeable.
